blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.why: **подводить** (the infinitive) (to bring closer) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **подвести**. — Wiktionary, «подводить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **подводить**: to bring closer; to place (under); to substantiate (with), to support (with), to account (for by); to class, to group together, to present (as), to depict (as).  «The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. However, many of the prefixed verbs have also secondary meanings, some of which are more important than the basic meanings.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «под- — Подвезти – give someone a lift: Он подвёз меня до центра. — He took me (as far as) downtown.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: I don't want to let him down.
exercises.context: The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. (DLI, Lesson 79)

exercises.why: **пройду** is the future tense (1st person singular) of **пройти** (to pass, to go, to walk; to pass by) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проходить**. future: я пройду́ · ты пройдёшь · он пройдёт · мы пройдём · вы пройдёте · они пройду́т. — Wiktionary, «пройти» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. Мы прошли мимо станции метро. — We passed the metro station. Prepositional phrases: сквозь / через / в + acc.; мимо + gen.; without preposition.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «The prefix "про-" implies the following meanings: a) Going through — через + Acc.: Мы проехали через лес. b) Passing by — мимо + Gen.: Мы прошли мимо вашего дома. c) Passing between — между + Instr.: Войска противника прошли между лесом и рекой. d) Covering a distance — verb + Acc.: Они прошли два километра. e) Passing (missing) a place or leaving it behind — verb + Acc.: Мы проехали нашу станцию. (missed it) Мы уже проехали этот город. (left it behind) Notice also the following expressions: Прошла неделя. — A week went by. Дождь прошёл. — The rain stopped.» — DLI, Lesson 62.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Excuse me. May I get by?
exercises.context: **про-** — Movement across, through, or past something Example: Мы проехали через город. — We drove through the city. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **расходиться** (the infinitive) (to go away, to disperse (in different directions), to spread; to break up (of a crowd, meeting, etc.)) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **разойтись**. — Wiktionary, «расходиться» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся)** — Divergent movement in various directions from one center. Antonym: с-, со- (+сь, +ся) Example: Дед Мороз разнёс подарки по домам. — Grandfather Frost brought the gifts to the (various) houses. После ужина, мы разошлись по домам. — After dinner, we went to our separate homes. Prepositional phrases: по + dat. pl.; в + acc. pl.» — Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0).  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
exercises.prompt: Rumors began to spread.
exercises.context: **раз-, разо-, рас- (+сь, +ся)** — Divergent movement in various directions from one center. (Wikipedia, «Russian grammar» § Verbs of motion (CC BY-SA 4.0))

exercises.why: **провёл** is the past tense (masculine) of **провести** (to lead, to conduct, to guide, to steer, to take) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проводить**. past: он провёл · она провела́ · оно провело́ · они провели́. — Wiktionary, «провести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **провести**: to lead, to conduct, to guide, to steer, to take; to lay, to construct, to build, to install a road, a pipe, a wire etc.; to carry out, to carry through, to realize, to put into practice, to conduct; to pass over, to run over.  «The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. However, many of the prefixed verbs have also secondary meanings, some of which are more important than the basic meanings.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «Проводить — провести — to lead through, to spend (time), to lay (a road). Note the expression: "проводить время" — to spend the time.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).

exercises.why: **уходить** (the infinitive) (to leave, to depart, to go (away) (by foot); to escape, to evade) — imperfective; its perfective partner is **уйти**. — Wiktionary, «уходить» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  «**у-** — Intended departure, signals absence. exercises.why: **проведём** is the future tense (1st person plural) of **провести** (to lead, to conduct, to guide, to steer, to take) — perfective; its imperfective partner is **проводить**. future: я проведу́ · ты проведёшь · он проведёт · мы проведём · вы проведёте · они проведу́т. — Wiktionary, «провести» (CC BY-SA 4.0).  Wiktionary's senses of **провести**: to lead, to conduct, to guide, to steer, to take; to lay, to construct, to build, to install a road, a pipe, a wire etc.; to carry out, to carry through, to realize, to put into practice, to conduct; to pass over, to run over.  «The verbs "носить", "возить" and "водить" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. However, many of the prefixed verbs have also secondary meanings, some of which are more important than the basic meanings.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  «Проводить — провести — to lead through, to spend (time), to lay (a road). Note the expression: "проводить время" — to spend the time.» — DLI, Lesson 79.  ·  Sentence and translation from Tatoeba (CC BY 2.0 FR).
